relationships.description: Apple Inc. operates the App Store.
Apple Inc. has App Review Guidelines.
California District Court found that certain provisions of Apple Inc.’s App Review Guidelines violate California’s unfair competition law.
California District Court issued the 2021 Injunction.

2021 Injunction enjoins Apple Inc. from prohibiting developers from including buttons, external links, or other calls to action that direct customers to purchasing mechanisms other than the Company’s in-app purchase system.
California District Court issued the 2025 Injunction.

2025 Injunction enjoins Apple Inc. from imposing commission or fee on purchases outside an app, restricting how developers guide consumers to purchases outside an app, or otherwise interfering with consumer choice.

relationships.target: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
relationships.description: Apple Inc. appealed the California District Court’s April 2025 decision to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit.
Ninth Circuit Court upheld the 2025 Injunction in part and modified certain aspects.
Ninth Circuit Court allowed Apple Inc. to require parity in size, form and placement between the in-app purchase and any links for consumers to make purchases outside an app.
Ninth Circuit Court held that Apple Inc. can charge some commission on link-out purchases.
Ninth Circuit Court remanded to the California District Court to further amend or modify the 2025 Injunction.
Apple Inc. filed a petition seeking Supreme Court review of the Ninth Circuit Court’s opinion.
Supreme Court granted Apple Inc.’s petition to review the applicable legal standard for civil contempt.
Apple Inc. is seeking a stay of the California District Court proceedings pending the Supreme Court’s decision.
Apple Inc. is subject to other legal proceedings and claims.
Apple Inc. settled certain matters during the third quarter of 2026.
Apple Inc. depends on obtaining components and computing resources.
Apple Inc. currently obtains certain components from single or limited sources.
Apple Inc. is experiencing a period of supply constraints and increasing costs for components.
Apple Inc. has risk factors described in the 2025 Form 10-K and second quarter 2026 Form 10-Q.
Apple Inc. has an in-app purchase system.
